title: The Price of a Dream

full_text:
Riding through the dusty lanes on his trusty gray donkey—often sitting backward so he could keep an eye on where he had been—Mulla Nasruddin was approached by the local villagers. A miserly merchant brought a poor weaver before the court, shouting: "Last night I dreamed that this pauper broke into my storehouse and stole ten sacks of flour! He must pay me fi.... The local folk, who never missed an opportunity to hear the Mulla’s unexpected pronouncements, quickly formed an expectant circle around him, stroking their beards and whispering among themselves.

Seeing everyone staring at him with grave expressions, Nasruddin adjusted his voluminous turban with theatrical dignity. A crowd of curious onlookers gathered in a circle, eagerly anticipating how the Mulla would resolve the impossible dilemma. Rather than offering a conventional, boring answer that any dry scholar might recite, the Mulla approached the problem from an angle that no one in the village had ever dreamed possible.

With effortless timing and a completely straight face, Nasruddin delivered his masterstroke: With deadpan gravity and a twinkle in his eye, Nasruddin delivered his unforgettable verdict.  The entire square erupted into bewildered chuckles and hearty laughter, leaving the bewildered questioners shaking their heads in admiration, proving that an imaginary injury deserves nothing more than an imaginary compensation.
moral: An imaginary injury deserves nothing more than an imaginary compensation.
